name: UIA-IOT-IDS dataset: Comprehensive IoT network intrusion detection and sensor-anomaly
description: This record contains two complementary, fully labelled datasets for machine-learning-based IoT security, together with the complete acquisition and analysis code. All data were collected from a single physical smart-home testbed at the University of Agder (Grimstad, Norway), built around a resource-constrained Raspberry Pi 3 gateway, five ESP8266 + DHT22 temperature/humidity nodes in distinct rooms, a PySense board, a Flask IoT server with InfluxDB storage, and three Kali Linux attacker VMs. Network flows were computed on-device in real time by a custom tcpdump-based extractor, so no raw PCAP is stored. The deposit is organised into two datasets that serve two tasks: (1) IDS_Dataset - network-flow INTRUSION DETECTION. The "Original" folder holds the raw, as-collected flows: 3,637,408 labelled bidirectional records across 54 classes, each described by 75 columns (6 identifier/metadata fields + 69 statistical features) plus a label. Of the 69 features, 46 are schema-compatible with CIC-IoT-2023 and 23 are additional bidirectional descriptors (per-direction packet counts, packet-length and inter-arrival-time statistics, and flow rates). The "Balanced" folder holds a cleaned, SMOTE-balanced version: 1,415,074 records, one CSV per class, with identifier and zero-variance columns removed (64 features + label). The taxonomy spans 51 attack sub-types in nine categories - Reconnaissance, DoS, DDoS, Brute Force, Web-based, Mirai, Spoofing, False Data Injection and Backdoor/C2 - plus three benign traffic types (sensor, SSH, Grafana). It reproduces the eight CIC-IoT-2023 categories and adds families absent from common benchmarks: False Data Injection (direct injection and man-in-the-middle sensor replay) and Backdoor/command-and-control beaconing. (2) AD_Dataset - sensor ANOMALY DETECTION. The "Benign" folder holds timestamped temperature and humidity readings from the five DHT22 nodes (one CSV per node); the "Abnormal" folder holds readings from three anomaly sources: a heat-biased PySense board (hardware fault), direct false-data injection, and ARP-spoofing replay. 4,253,024 readings fall within the 1 March - 13 April 2026 window analysed in the article; earlier readings are also included. Each reading is stored as one row carrying either a temperature or a humidity value (InfluxDB export format). All tabular data are UTF-8 CSV files with a header row; every network-flow record carries an explicit label. The deposit also includes the full code: the real-time flow extractor, the Flask server with intentionally vulnerable endpoints, the attack and injection scripts, the SMOTE preprocessing, and the model code (XGBoost benchmark, LSTM-autoencoder, MAML, Prototypical Networks). A disjoint base/novel class split supports supervised, unsupervised and few-shot detection research.
